solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What a buccaneering student does in plot

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart, so what a student does is cons
buccaneering is the activity of piracy on the high seas

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a pirate-mad scholar gets up to.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'what a student of buccaneering does': he cons (studies) piracy.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret scheme, which is the meaning of a conspiracy.

clue.text: Player not yet big gun?

definitions.meaning: in sport a junior or inexperienced player is called a ...

explanation.definitionFit: A colt is both a young player in a team and a Colt revolver, a well-known handgun brand.

clue.text: Horse should have drink? Then it's little good going on and on!

parts.note: a nag is an old or poor horse
gin is a spirit, a drink
G is the short form of good

explanation.surface: A thirsty horse that keeps complaining about its lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagging is persistent complaining, someone going on and on at another person.

clue.text: Card mounting is obsolescent, a bit unfashionable

parts.note: passé means out of date, going out of use
a part is a bit of something
out means no longer in fashion

explanation.surface: A picture framer dismissing a style of mount as dated.
explanation.walkthrough: A passe-partout is a card mount or frame for a picture, held with tape.
explanation.definitionFit: A passe-partout is a cardboard mount used for framing pictures, so it is literally a card mounting.

clue.text: New serial about street folk who don't have fancy ideas?

definitions.text: folk who don't have fancy ideas?

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece encloses the other
new suggests the letters are made new, put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new serial set on a street about down-to-earth people.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a playful description rather than a dictionary one: realists have no fanciful ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Realists are practical people who accept things as they are, without fanciful notions.

clue.text: A hundred yobs — they're supposed to disappear in June?

definitions.text: they're supposed to disappear in June?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
yobs are louts, rough young men

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a hundred hooligans might vanish by midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'Ne'er cast a clout till May be out' means do not shed warm clothes (clouts) until the end of May, so by June they may go.
explanation.definitionFit: A clout is an old word for a garment; the proverb implies such warm clothes are shed once May is out.

clue.text: Instrument making note, first to blast off

indicators.note: the opening letter blasts off, so the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a sharp is a musical note raised a semitone

explanation.surface: A musician making a note before the first one blasts off.
explanation.definitionFit: The harp is a stringed musical instrument plucked with the fingers.

clue.text: A disreputable type getting first in English, this person in the university world

parts.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

indicators.note: first in picks out the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the setter referring to himself as this person means me

explanation.surface: A rogue gaining a first in English and joining academia.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe means the academic world, the environment of universities and scholarship.

clue.text: Province's head having introduced a language of bygone days

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: having introduced means one piece has another put inside it

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
Latin is the classical language of ancient Rome, no longer spoken

explanation.surface: A province's ruler bringing in an ancient tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A palatinate is a territory ruled by a count palatine, a type of province.

clue.text: One getting in on the act, so to speak

definitions.text: One getting in on the act, so to speak

parts.words: One getting in on the act, so to speak
parts.note: the idiom 'get in on the act' means join in, but read literally it is someone involved in making an Act of Parliament

explanation.definitionFit: Lawmakers draft and pass Acts, so they are literally involved in making the act.

clue.text: Everyone joining start of march from avenue

indicators.note: start of picks out the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: Everyone joining the start of a march down an avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: A mall is a broad tree-lined walk or avenue, as in The Mall in London.

clue.text: Smog is swirling with people showing evidence of frightening experience?

indicators.note: swirling letters are churned into a new order, like smog moving about

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: People in swirling smog showing signs of a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' rearranges SMOG IS plus PEOPLE; 'with' and 'showing' are joining words, and the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bumps on the skin appear when someone is scared or cold, a sign of fear.

clue.text: We will embrace one female who is not the mistress!

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A couple embracing a woman who is not the man's lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A married man's spouse is distinguished from his mistress, his lover outside marriage.

clue.text: Withdrawn type at home time and time again hugging dog

parts.note: at home means in

indicators.note: hugging means holding something inside, around it

parts.note: T again for the repeated time
T again for the repeated time
Rover is a stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: A shy person at home repeatedly cuddling the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time and time again' gives two Ts, which hug ROVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert is a reserved, inward-looking person, someone withdrawn.

clue.text: Eve and I cavort around, doing too much

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are thrown about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Two people dancing about wildly, overdoing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Overactive means excessively active, so doing more than is wise.

clue.text: Tramps making rude sign when accepting handout

parts.note: V is the two-fingered V-sign, a rude British gesture

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a grant is a handout of money

explanation.surface: Tramps giving the V-sign while taking money.
explanation.walkthrough: The V-sign, two fingers raised palm inward, is an insult in Britain, also called a Harvey Smith.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagrants are homeless wanderers, a synonym for tramps.

clue.text: Back from China maybe, first to leave

indicators.note: the first letter leaves, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: China is an example of something eastern, from the East

explanation.surface: Coming back from China, the first to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical term meaning backwards or at the back of a ship.

clue.text: Mostly the person with a book is someone needing a yarn?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: someone with a book is a reader

explanation.surface: A bookworm craving a good story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a story for the reader, but it is the thread put through a needle's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A threader puts thread or yarn through a needle, so needs yarn to work.

clue.text: Family including British people who are cold and mechanical

definitions.text: people who are cold and mechanical

indicators.note: including means holding something within

parts.note: roots are one's family origins

explanation.surface: A British family whose members are cold and unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Robots are machines, and figuratively people who act without warmth or feeling.

clue.text: Over a long time friendship can bring oppression

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed over another comes first

parts.note: a bond is a tie of friendship
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A long friendship leading to oppression.
explanation.definitionFit: Bondage is slavery or subjugation, a state of oppression.

clue.text: Bits of food, cooked — what may be provided by a golf club

definitions.text: what may be provided by a golf club

parts.note: chips are fried strips of potato
food just cooked is hot

explanation.surface: Hot chips on the menu at a golf clubhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf club' looks like the clubhouse serving the chips, but it is the club used to hit a short lofted shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A short lofted stroke onto the green is played with a golf club such as a wedge.

clue.text: Not quite the ideal situation, small house? Let's make an effort!

indicators.note: not quite means the final letter is cut

parts.note: heaven is an ideal state of bliss
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A tiny house that falls short of paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailors' cry when hauling together, urging everyone to pull hard.

clue.text: Deal successfully with two irregular verbs

parts.note: make is an irregular verb (made)
do is an irregular verb (did, done)

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson coping with two awkward verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage with what is at hand is to cope, dealing with a situation successfully enough.

clue.text: A cult one's contrived in diplomatic office

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A cult's plot hatched in an embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: A consulate is the office of a consul, a diplomatic post abroad.

clue.text: Copper perhaps losing heart? Food needed

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: copper is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: A policeman losing heart and needing food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman; here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal is an occasion of eating, an amount of food.

clue.text: Short artist turning up, well past his prime

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up reads the word from bottom to top
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Degas was a French painter

explanation.surface: A small painter getting past his best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' turns DEGAS into DEGA, which 'turning up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means old, well beyond one's best years.

clue.text: Troubled country? I question soldiers being sent in

indicators.note: being sent in means inserted within the other letters

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Asking about troops being deployed to a war-torn country.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a Middle Eastern country that has suffered much war and unrest.

clue.text: The man I guided round, composer from German city

parts.note: the man is he

indicators.note: round means turned about, read backwards

parts.note: guided means led
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: Showing a man round, then a composer from a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Heidelberg is a university city in southwestern Germany.

clue.text: Sheep approaching river vessel

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep heading for the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug or pitcher, a container for water.

clue.text: Agree to provide answer after expression of surprise

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
to respond is to provide an answer

explanation.surface: Agreeing to reply after an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things correspond when they agree or match each other.
